ops.body:
Verdict (2026-08-03, daemonkit v0.21 migration): changing the struct hashed by
`terminalOutcomeDigest` (`internal/accountterminal/terminal.go`) is NOT a
durable-format break. No path recomputes a terminal outcome digest from live
state and compares it against a stored one.

This was gating: the v0.21 migration retyped `proc.Record`, one of the four
fields hashed (`{kind, exit_code, signal, record}`). Two lanes checked it
independently and a third pass confirmed. Migration has since landed
(`6ef80b4` + `216a84f`) and the retype is done — `TerminalOutcome.Record
proc.Record` became `PID int`, `Terminal.Record()` became `Terminal.PID()`.

## The structural proof (strongest form)

`internal/accountterminal`'s only external imports are **daemonkit's root
package and creack/pty**. No store, no journal, no durable, no encoding target.
The package cannot persist anything and cannot put anything on the wire, so no
call-site census is needed to rule out a durable break: it is unrepresentable.

(Pre-migration the same argument held in a weaker form — the sole external
import was `daemonkit/proc`.)

Re-verify this by reading the import block, not by re-walking callers. An
import that can write to disk or encode for the wire is the one change that
would reopen the question.

## The trap: `outcome_digest` is a NAME COLLISION

The persisted `outcome_digest` column (`internal/store/store.go`, receipt field
`internal/store/account_mutation.go:135`) is a DIFFERENT digest. It is typed
`store.CredentialDigest` and covers credential state, not terminal outcome.
Every daemon write site passes `ExpectedCredentialDigest` or `state.Digest()`
(`internal/daemon/account_mutation.go:181,664,1222,1249`), and the store's
recompute-and-compare paths (`internal/store/account_mutation.go:1011,1018,
1128-1133`) recompute from credential `Observation.Digest()`.
`TerminalOutcome.Digest` never flows into the store.

Reading the column name as "the terminal outcome's digest" is the single most
likely way to get this question wrong, in either direction.

## Supporting facts

- Computed once at settlement, stored only in the in-memory `t.result`, which
  is never serialized.
- Only comparison is `Acknowledge` against a caller-echoed copy. The single
  non-test caller is `internal/daemon/account_mutation.go:62`, echoing a value
  it got from `Wait` in the same process. Terminal outcomes do not survive a
  daemon restart, so an old-format and a new-format digest can never meet.
- Never on the wire: `internal/daemon/protocol.go` carries only
  `store.CredentialDigest` fields.
- Zero golden/testdata files in the repo. `TestTerminalOutcomeDigestBindsCompleteRecord`
  (`internal/accountterminal/terminal_test.go`) is a SENSITIVITY test — two
  records must hash differently — not a golden pin, so it survives a format
  change and is evidence in neither direction. Post-migration it binds PID
  identity rather than record identity.
- The v0.20.9 goldens in `internal/store/upgrade_fixture_test.go` pin
  `owner_record` bytes, unrelated to this digest.

## What would invalidate this

`internal/accountterminal` growing an import that can write to disk or encode
for the wire; `TerminalOutcome.Digest` being added to a protocol message; or
terminal state being made to survive a daemon restart. Check the import block
first — it is the cheapest signal.
